summary: Took the step the last interpretation said was needed: the sweep now emits the operands of each rejected apply, so a receipt can carry the offending entry instead of only a count. Draft-side the run names it exactly, and it is the same entry in all three occurrences - index 4, term 2, one change, JointImplicit - rejected by three different nodes (3, 1, 4) at seed 35, steps 22, 23 and 31, each time with the node reporting applied=4, committed=4 and joint_now=true, against 245 configuration changes, 446 restarts, 481 elections, 51 unapplied-change check points and violations=0. That is a sharper picture than the count: the entry that trips the Changer is a single joint-entering change at one log position applied by several nodes, so the shape is not merely one lagging node seeing a change out of order - it invites the question of whether a leave entry should have preceded index 4 and whether the proposer was entitled to append it, which the operands alone do not answer. I deliberately stop short of interpreting it because the operands are draft-side only, so the submission requests isolated execution of these bytes with the new instrumentation described (up to three invalid_change_apply events carrying seed, step, node, entry index, entry term, change count, joint flag, applied, committed and joint_now; the summary keeps invalid_change_applies and invalid_change_reasons), and states in the assumptions that the operands describe the entry and node state at rejection but do not establish the proposer's entitlement, that only the first three occurrences are emitted while the counter counts all, and that the numbers are descriptive rather than rates. Next step after the receipt: print the surrounding log entries for that index so the ordering question can be settled rather than argued.
